claim_text: Safety evidence for concentrated turmeric/curcumin supplements during pregnancy and breastfeeding is insufficient to support routine supplement-dose recommendations; culinary use should not be equated with concentrated extracts or enhanced-bioavailability formulations.
health_goal_or_outcome: Avoid unsupported concentrated turmeric/curcumin supplement recommendations during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

population.health_status: Pregnant or lactating people considering supplements.
population.other_context: Product concentration, formulation and co-ingredients matter.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Concentrated turmeric/curcumin extracts and enhanced-bioavailability formulations; distinguish from culinary spice use.
comparator: Culinary food use versus concentrated supplement exposure.
evidence_summary: NCCIH Turmeric page summarizes evidence and safety limitations; pregnancy-specific data for concentrated supplement products are limited.
limitations: Insufficient evidence is not proof of harm or safety.
Do not generalize culinary use to supplements.
Professional review is required for pregnancy/lactation and medication interactions.
